title: Builds, deployment and rollback
objectives: Apply a bounded pure canary error-count gate with explicit eligible populations, minimum evidence and strict excess-error threshold without claiming significance or automatic deployment authority.
Check declared read/write schema rollback compatibility and explain immutable artifacts, staged rollout, migration/backup evidence and irreversible data limits.
Apply builds, deployment and rollback invariants safely and identify scope boundaries.
motivation: A release binds reviewed source/build artifact digest, dependency/config/schema versions, migration plan, test evidence, environment, owner/authority, observation and rollback/restore. Build once and promote the same verified artifact rather than rebuilding unrecorded variations.

blocks.md: A release binds reviewed source/build artifact digest, dependency/config/schema versions, migration plan, test evidence, environment, owner/authority, observation and rollback/restore. Build once and promote the same verified artifact rather than rebuilding unrecorded variations. A hash identifies bytes, not trusted build provenance or correctness. This lesson deploys nothing and purchases no service. A local gate can only evaluate supplied evidence, not grant authority or replace actual mobile/app/runtime/production tests.

Google SRE defines canarying as partial, time-limited deployment/evaluation against a control. Predefine population, traffic assignment, window, user-impact metrics, minimum evidence, stop/reset/escalation and observation duration. Unequal or contaminated traffic can bias comparisons; errors alone miss latency/data/security regressions. Low traffic or rare failures may require longer/more targeted tests, not automatic promotion because no error was seen.

blocks.title: Error gate and schema rollback are different checks
items: Own control 1 bad/1000, canary 10/1000 has excess 9/1000=.009, above allowed 1/200=.005, so stop-investigate. Canary 0/10 has insufficient events for minimum 100, so hold, not success.
Canary 2/1000 versus 1/1000 has excess .001 and is eligible-for-next-reviewed-step ONLY. This descriptive threshold is not a hypothesis test, confidence bound or live rollout permission.

Database schema 2 cannot safely roll back to v1 declared read/write support {1}. A bridge artifact supporting both {1,2} passes that one compatibility check. Caller declarations must be backed by actual mixed-version read/write tests; no data migration or deployment happens here.

blocks.caption: Expected stop-investigate; hold-insufficient-evidence; eligible-for-next-reviewed-step; False; True. Complete pure Fraction counts/gate and declared read/write schema check. Strict excess>threshold; equal threshold passes only this descriptive rule. No CI/test significance, traffic routing, artifact authentication, migration, rollback/restore execution or full release approval.

blocks.md: A binary rollback does not reverse database writes or recover dropped columns. Google's release guidance describes a bridge version that tolerates the new schema before enabling new features. Expand/migrate/contract introduces new structure, backfills/verifies, changes compatible readers/writers, then removes old structure only after consumers have moved and recovery implications are understood. Dual-write consistency and new data not representable in old schema need explicit reconciliation; the pattern is not automatically zero downtime or fully reversible.

Preserve known-good artifact/configuration and verify it can read AND write the current schema/data without corruption. Define traffic drain, queued requests, in-flight unknown outcomes, compatibility/feature flags and postrollback checks. Destructive/irreversible migrations may require forward fix or a tested restore with explicit data-loss/recovery-point consequences; do not blindly deploy an old binary. Restore authorization/data loss cannot be inferred from a generic request to make an app work.

Tests should bind actual artifact/revision/environment: unit/property/reference, contract/integration, migration/mixed-version, security/dependency, resource/performance, renderer/mobile/a11y/user flows and recovery. A source curriculum archive or green classroom gate is not deployed production evidence. Canary only after appropriate predeployment tests, with limited authorized exposure and monitoring; not a replacement for those tests. Stop on unexplained regressions and retain evidence instead of removing behavior to pass checks.

Google SRE release/canary guidance describes practices and tradeoffs, not a universal recipe or approval for this user's accounts. Liquibase describes expand/migrate/contract; actual engine/transaction/locking/backfill behavior depends on database and migration tools. This own descriptive count gate and declared schema sets are deliberately narrow, no framework or platform is installed.

Independent transfer: enumerate small canary/control counts, compare exact rational differences and test empty/minimum/equality boundaries. Construct v1/bridge/v2 read/write compatibility tables and reject read-only support when writes are needed. Design a schema-drop scenario where binary rollback is unsafe, and state forward-fix/restore choices with data-loss/authority gaps. Record outstanding actual app/production tests rather than invent a deployed success.

Sources: [Google SRE canarying](https://sre.google/workbook/canarying-releases/), [reliable releases/rollback and bridge schema](https://cloud.google.com/blog/products/gcp/reliable-releases-and-rollbacks-cre-life-lessons), [Liquibase expand/contract](https://www.liquibase.com/technical-glossary/expand-contract-pattern), [incident mitigation context](https://sre.google/workbook/incident-response/). Own gate thresholds and compatibility records are synthetic, not current vendor policy or deployment commands.

guidedExercise.prompt: What must be known before rolling back after a destructive database migration?
hints: Distinguishes binary rollback and restore/forward fix.
guidedExercise.solution: Current schema/data and old artifact read/write compatibility, irreversible/lost data, new writes, queues/unknown effects, known-good artifact/config, forward-fix versus tested restore/recovery-point/time/data-loss and explicit operational authority. Need actual environment checks, not pure set declarations or old binary label.

independentExercise.prompt: Write a small test case that deliberately breaks the contract boundary in "Builds, deployment and rollback" and verify how your implementation rejects or handles it.
hints: Test zero, negative, empty, duplicate, and boundary values.
Confirm both time/memory complexity and numerical precision remain within spec.

commonMistakes: Minimum evidence and outcome ratio differ. (No-error small sample is not proof.)
Compatibility is more than successful read parsing. (Mixed-version write semantics need real tests.)
realWorldApplication: Used directly across production quantitative research, execution systems, and validation pipelines.
quantFinanceApplication: Applies rigorous engineering contracts to quantitative modeling and live trading infrastructure.
summary: A release needs bound artifact/config/schema/evidence and authorized staged operations.
A small error-only canary gate is descriptive evidence, not automatic approval.
Binary rollback depends on current read/write data/schema compatibility and cannot undo irreversible migrations or restore lost data by itself.

quiz.prompt: A canary has 0 errors in 10 events but minimum 100 is required. What happens?
quiz.explanation: Minimum evidence and outcome ratio differ. (No-error small sample is not proof.)

quiz.prompt: Old binary reads schema 2 but cannot write it safely. Can this declared compatibility check pass?
options: Yes, if its name is known-good
quiz.explanation: Compatibility is more than successful read parsing. (Mixed-version write semantics need real tests.)

quiz.prompt: Canary 10/1000 minus control 1/1000 has excess numerator over 1000 what?

quiz.explanation: Avoid turning a gate label into a broader claim. (Other evidence and authority remain required.)

quiz.prompt: Why can dropping an old column make rollback unsafe?
options: Rolling back the binary automatically restores the dropped column and its data
Old code/data assumptions may no longer hold
quiz.explanation: Schema/data reversibility needs explicit evidence. (Binary rollback does not recreate lost data.)
